newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq index ends at new high; Dow ekes out gain.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq index ends at new high; Dow ekes out gain.

text.p: Stocks ended higher Monday, with technology stocks extending their torrid run and blue chips scratching out slender gains.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 1.16 points at 7,922.98.
The Nasdaq index rose 21.26 points to 1,523.88, extending its streak of consecutive record closes to eight, as investors flocked to the suddenly sizzling tech sector.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,471 to 1,375 on moderate volume of 485 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The tech stocks face a critical series of earnings-related tests this week, with reports due from industry bellwether companies Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp.

"We get Intel tomorrow and Microsoft on Thursday," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management, "and this trend could either break or continue right on, based on what those two companies say."

Intel warned in late May that its second quarter earnings would fall short of earlier forecasts due to product transition issues. Investors have apparently decided the worst is already passed, analysts said.
"Right now, the market is certainly telling us it expects good news," Truicko said.
Intel rose 1-7/8 to 78-3/4, and Microsoft surged 6-3/16 to 135-15/16.
At the same time tech stocks have shot higher, the Dow has stalled a bit, remaining stuck just below the 8,000 mark since closing at 7,895.81 on July 3.
While analysts are not expecting a stiff blue chip correction, they say the milestone may remain elusive for a while longer, as investors flock to the once again favoured technology group.

"Many players in the large caps were there for the short term and they don't want to be buying here, when a lot of those stocks are quite expensive," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
"On the other hand, a lot of the techs had been neglected or just overlooked," she said. "Once they started going up, people just got more comfortable with them again."
The quarterly corporate earnings season started in earnest Monday, with a flurry of banking companies that reported profits in line with or slightly above Wall Street forecasts.
Among banks reporting were NationsBank Corp., which rose 11/16 to close at 67-5/16, First Chicago NBD Corp., which rose 7/16 to 63-7/16, and Bank of New York Corp., which closed up 1/4 at 46-1/8.
Investment bank Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. jumped 1-7/8 to 58-15/16 after reporting strong earnings.
Health care information provider HCIA Inc. plummeted 16-3/8 to 15-5/8 after warning it expected a second quarter loss.
Chemical producer DuPont Co. fell 15/16 to 62-5/16 after announcing an agreement to buy several chemical businesses from Imperial Chemical Industries Plc for $3 billion.
American Depositary shares in Imperial Chemical rose 3-5/8 to 59-7/8.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 1.70 points to 918.38. The American Stock Exchange index was off 2.84 to 632.63.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.01 to 478.11. The average share was unchanged.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 8,701.104, up 18.407, or 0.21 percent.
